content: The community-based ART (antiretroviral therapy) tool includes the following key components for patient management: 1. Facility and Community Health Worker (CHW) Information: The tool records the name of the facility, district, CHW's name, contact number, village, and district. It also tracks the dates when the register was started and completed. 2. Patient Identification and Contact Details: Each patient is assigned a unique ID, and their first name, last name, phone number, and address are documented. If a patient moves out of the CHW's catchment area, the date and new location are recorded. Additionally, the date of death is noted if applicable. 3. Visit and Treatment Details: The tool logs the date of each visit, the date the patient started their ARV regimen, the number of pills remaining, the date pills were dispensed, the quantity dispensed, and the date of the next refill. Any treatment interruptions are recorded, including the dates and reasons for the interruptions. 4. Treatment Interruption Reasons: Common reasons for interruptions include: Severe illness or hospitalization. Drug stockouts. Financial constraints faced by the patient. Poor adherence to the treatment regimen. Other reasons, which must be specified. 5. Assessment of Tuberculosis (TB) Symptoms: At every visit, patients are assessed for TB symptoms, including: Current cough. Fever. Weight loss. Night sweats. If any symptoms are present, the patient is referred for testing and treatment. 6. Other Health Problems: The tool also tracks other health issues, such as: Ankle swelling. Puffiness of the face. Breathlessness. Diarrhea lasting more than two weeks. 7. Pregnancy and Family Planning: The tool identifies whether the patient is pregnant or using family planning methods. If the patient is pregnant, has TB symptoms, or other health problems, the referral date is recorded. 8. Documentation: Each patient is assigned to a single register page for detailed tracking.
